composition: The nominal composition is Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C (at.%): Fe as balance, 15 at.% Al, 2 at.% Nb, and 1 at.% C. The matrix is an A2 bcc disordered Fe-Al solid solution; at 15 at.% Al the matrix remains disordered A2 up to the melting temperature, in contrast to Fe-26Al-based alloys which undergo D03/B2 and B2/A2 order-disorder transitions. Nb and C are added with the intent of forming fine NbC carbide strengthening precipitates in the Fe-Al matrix.
conclusions: Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C is a two-phase as-cast iron aluminide in which a fine NbC carbide dispersion strongly strengthens the A2 Fe-Al matrix: it attains a matrix hardness of 309 HB and a room-temperature compressive yield stress of 827 MPa, and, together with the Ta-containing analogue, shows the highest strengthening among the Fe-15Al-based alloys at every tested temperature up to 800 °C. The alloy is nevertheless brittle at room temperature (transgranular cleavage, with tensile yield stress and elongation not measurable), and its strength falls monotonically with temperature without a yield-stress anomaly, collapsing steeply between about 600 and 800 °C to 0-100 MPa. Tension-compression asymmetry persists at room temperature and at 650/800 °C. Overall, Nb and C additions impart promising high-temperature strength to Fe-15Al-based alloys, but room-temperature ductility remains a limitation.
mechanisms: The 2 at.% Nb and 1 at.% C additions form fine, sub-micrometre (<1 um) granular/lamellar NbC carbides in eutectic regions of the A2 bcc Fe-Al matrix; these hard, coarsening-resistant MC carbides provide precipitation strengthening that raises the matrix hardness to 309 HB and the room-temperature compressive yield stress to 827 MPa, far above the binary Fe-15Al reference (159 HB, 356 MPa).

Because the Fe-15Al matrix remains A2 bcc disordered up to the melting temperature (with no D03/B2 order-disorder transitions), Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C shows a monotonic decrease in compressive yield stress with increasing temperature rather than the yield-stress anomaly exhibited by Fe-26Al-based alloys.

In room-temperature compression the alloy deforms with parabolic work hardening typical of disordered polycrystalline metals, and the dense fine NbC dispersion produces one of the steepest hardening curves among the Fe-15Al-based alloys.

The higher compressive than tensile yield stress (tension-compression asymmetry) is attributed to the nonplanar core of screw dislocations in the bcc matrix, to internal stresses arising from the different elastic properties of matrix and carbide phase during solidification (Bauschinger effect), and to notch sensitivity of the matrix induced by the carbide precipitates.

The brittle room-temperature failure occurs by coarse transgranular cleavage (TGC) with elongated plates visible on the fracture surface, consistent with the abrupt, low-ductility load drop observed in tension.
microstructure: The as-cast microstructure is two-phase: a dendritic Fe-Al matrix with A2 bcc disordered crystal structure, present as equiaxed (30 um) and columnar (30x80 um) dendrites, together with NbC carbide precipitates smaller than 1 um that appear granular and lamellar within eutectic regions. The NbC forms the main strengthening precipitate phase and shares phase interfaces with the Fe-Al matrix.
processing: The alloy was processed by vacuum induction melting and cast into cylindrical copper moulds (32 mm diameter x 186 mm length); no further heat treatment is reported, so the material is characterised in the as-cast state. Specimens were cut by spark erosion along the longitudinal axis of the ingot (casting direction) and their surfaces ground. Compression samples measured (6x6x10) mm^3, and flat tensile samples had a (3.5x5) mm^2 cross-section with a 15 mm gauge length.
properties: The Brinell hardness of the matrix is 309 HB (2.5 mm diameter indentation ball; reported load 62.5 g). At room temperature and a deformation rate of 10^-4 s^-1, the compressive yield stress is 827 MPa, and the compression stress-strain curve shows parabolic work hardening, being among the steepest of the Fe-15Al-based alloys and terminating just below the 1400 MPa gridline. In room-temperature tension the alloy is brittle: the stress-strain curve shows linear elastic loading followed by an abrupt load drop, peaking around the 500 MPa gridline, and both the tensile yield stress and total elongation are reported as '-' (not obtainable). Fracture occurs by transgranular cleavage (TGC); SEM fractography shows coarse transgranular cleavage facets with elongated plates. In elevated-temperature compression (up to 800 °C, protective argon, 30 min hold, NiCr-Ni thermocouple), the compressive yield stress lies between 800 and 900 MPa at the lowest test temperature and decreases monotonically with increasing temperature, collapsing steeply between about 600 and 800 °C and converging to 0-100 MPa by 800 °C; no yield-stress anomaly is observed. At 650 °C the compressive yield stress is roughly 350-450 MPa, with the tensile value lower, and at 800 °C compression again exceeds tension, confirming tension-compression asymmetry at room temperature and elevated temperatures. Characterisation methods comprised Brinell hardness, uniaxial compression and tension testing on a ZWICK 1474 universal testing machine at 10^-4 s^-1, and SEM fractography (Hitachi S-530, 20 kV, working distance 15 mm, secondary electrons).
summary: Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C is a quaternary iron aluminide (nominal Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C, at.%) studied in the as-cast condition to assess the strengthening effect of NbC carbides on the room-temperature and elevated-temperature mechanical behaviour of Fe-15Al-based alloys with an A2 bcc disordered matrix.
